title: Building with 3-D shapes
keyIdea: A composite shape is a new solid made by joining smaller 3-D shapes. A rocket can be 2 cylinders with a cone on top; a lighthouse can be a cuboid, a cylinder and a cone. Each part keeps its own 3-D name: a cone is not a triangle and a cylinder is not a circle, because circles and triangles are flat. Flat faces can hold another shape, but nothing sits on the point of a cone, so a cone goes on top. Small cubes make new shapes too: 2 cubes in a row make a cuboid, and 8 cubes (2 long, 2 wide, 2 tall) make a bigger cube.
familyTip: Raid the recycling: a cereal box (cuboid), a tin (cylinder), a dice or sugar cube (cube) and an ice-cream cone or party hat (cone). Build a rocket, a castle or a robot together, then take turns to say what it is made of, from the bottom up. Use a few toy bricks to test: do 2 cubes in a row make a bigger cube?

visual.caption: Flat shape or solid shape? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: stack solids to copy a plan, name each part, fill spaces with cubes to make a cuboid and a bigger cube, check a robot, free build.

kid: You can join shapes to make a new shape. A rocket can be two cylinders with a cone on top. We call the new shape a model.
Each part still has its own name. A tin shape is a cylinder. A party hat shape is a cone. A box shape is a cuboid, and a dice shape is a cube.
Do not call them circles or triangles. A circle is flat, like a drawing. A cone is solid. You can pick it up and hold it.
Flat faces can hold a block. A cone has a point, so it goes on top. Two cubes in a row make a cuboid. Eight cubes can make a bigger cube.
adult: Ages 6 to 7. US Common Core 1.G.A.2 asks children to compose three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones and right circular cylinders) to create a composite shape, and to compose new shapes from it. England's Year 1 and Year 2 geometry asks them to recognise and name cubes, cuboids, cylinders and cones. Key words: 3-D shape, solid, cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone, face, flat, curved, composite shape.

Composing is the solid version of building a picture from pattern blocks. Children choose parts with a purpose (a flat face to build on, a cone to finish a tower), describe a model by its parts, and see that joined parts can form a new named solid: two cubes side by side make a cuboid, and eight make a cube twice as long in every direction.

Common mistakes: using flat names for solids (a cone is a triangle, a cylinder is a circle) because the side view looks flat; calling two joined cubes a bigger cube; counting only the cubes they can see in a stack; and trying to balance something on the point of a cone.

In the lab your child copies three plan cards by stacking solids from the bottom up, names each part of a pencil, a robot and a tower block (circle and triangle are on offer as traps), fills dashed spaces with small cubes to make two cuboids and a bigger cube with one cube hidden at the back, checks a robot made of solids, and then builds a model of their own.

practice.prompt: Sam builds a tower of {a} cubes and puts a cone on top. How many 3-D shapes did he use?
practice.hint: Count the cubes, then count the cone as one more shape.
practice.explain: {a} cubes and 1 cone make {=a+1} shapes. Every part of a model counts as its own shape.

practice.prompt: A cuboid is made of {a} cubes in a row. Ben adds {b} more cubes to the end of the row. How many cubes long is it now?
practice.hint: The row gets longer by one cube for each cube he adds.
practice.explain: {a} cubes and {b} more make {=a+b} cubes in a row. It is still a cuboid, just a longer one.

practice.prompt: What 3-D shape is a tin of beans?
practice.hint: It has a curved side and a flat circle at each end.
practice.explain: A tin is a cylinder. A circle is flat, but a tin is solid: you can hold it.

practice.prompt: Push 2 cubes together, end to end. What new shape do you get?
practice.hint: Is it as tall as it is long?
practice.explain: It is 2 cubes long but only 1 cube tall, so it is a cuboid, not a cube.

practice.prompt: You build a tower from a cube, a cylinder and a cone. Which one goes on top?
practice.hint: Which shape has a point that nothing can sit on?
practice.explain: A cone has a point, so nothing can sit on it. It goes on top of the tower.

pool.prompt: A rocket is {a} cylinders with 1 cone on top. How many shapes is the rocket made of?
pool.hint: Count the cylinders, then add the cone.
pool.explain: {a} cylinders and 1 cone make {=a+1} shapes in the rocket.

pool.prompt: A model has {a} layers of cubes. Each layer has 4 cubes. How many cubes is that?
pool.hint: Count in 4s, one 4 for each layer. Some cubes may be hidden at the back.
pool.explain: {a} layers of 4 cubes make {=4*a} cubes, even if you cannot see them all.

pool.prompt: What shape is the sharp end of a pencil?
pool.hint: It is solid, with a curved side and a point.
pool.explain: The tip is a cone. It looks like a triangle from the side, but a triangle is flat.

pool.prompt: Which shape has 6 flat faces that are all the same square?
pool.hint: A dice is this shape: every face is the same.
pool.explain: A cube has 6 square faces that are all the same. A cuboid can have long rectangle faces.

pool.prompt: Which shape is best at the bottom of a tower?
pool.hint: The bottom part needs a flat face to hold the next part.
pool.explain: A cuboid has flat faces, so it holds a block. A ball rolls and a cone has a point.

pool.prompt: A lighthouse is a cuboid, a cylinder and a cone. Which part is at the very top?
pool.hint: Which part has a point that nothing can sit on?
pool.explain: The cone is at the top: its point cannot hold anything above it.

pool.prompt: A drum is a cylinder. What shape are its two flat faces?
pool.hint: Look at the top of a tin or a drum.
pool.explain: A cylinder has a flat circle face at each end and a curved side between them.

pool.prompt: How many small cubes make a cube that is 2 long, 2 wide and 2 tall?
pool.hint: Count the bottom layer, then the top layer. Count the hidden ones too.
pool.explain: 4 cubes on the bottom and 4 on top make 8. One cube at the back is hidden.
